ai.description: This slender, thread-like snake reaches 15–20 cm. It is uniformly dark brown to black with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include a blunt, rounded head and a highly polished, cylindrical body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops filiformis* is best distinguished by its exceptionally slender, thread-like body and a distinct, sharply pointed, spine-tipped tail.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlops filiformis* inhabits moist leaf litter and soil within tropical evergreen forests and plantations, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The File Worm Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops filiformis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 2–4 elongated eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlops filiformis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
